I feel like my question is misguided because it does not answer the original question and seems to confuse the concepts of determinism and convergence to determinism, which are entirely different things. As an example, think of a game of tic-tac-toe where the players only know the positions of the pieces on their own side of the board. There is no way to know if the next move is going to come from the player on the left or the right, hence the game is perfectly random. However, each move can be predicted with a 100% probability, hence the game is deterministic. You can also see that the game can be made completely random by giving each player a pair of dice that is completely independent of the other dice.
Now, if the game were to be played by two players with perfect information about each other's moves, the game would still be deterministic because the players can build their best strategy. However, if the game were played by a human player, it would no longer be deterministic because that player would no longer have perfect information about the other player's strategy. So, a game with perfect information about the opponent's strategy is deterministic if the opponent has perfect information about the opponent's strategy. But that is not the point. The point is that the human player is not able to build a strategy because that would require them to understand how their opponent's moves are built, which is an absurd impossibility for a human player to do. A human player is unable to understand how a game of tic-tac-toe is constructed, but a computer can do so because they can build an artificial intelligence that can understand the game. And that is how the human player would come to have a 100% chance of winning any game of tic-tac-toe, even if their opponent had perfect information about their strategy.
